authentication_transport: Reading needs no sign-in. submit_proposal signed in through GitHub (OAuth 2.1 with PKCE; the token travels only in the HTTP Authorization: Bearer header, never in tool arguments) posts the Islet Improvement Proposal (IIP) straight away. Without a token it stages the checked draft and returns a one-click link to the pre-filled form at https://openislet.org/submit. GitHub is the only sign-in. ORCID iD, X handle and a display name are optional text fields, shown as typed and never as verified (docs/connector/QUEUE-API.md).
gatekeeper_blind_review_prompt_template: You are reviewing a proposed contribution to OpenIslet (https://openislet.org) under [OPENISLET-REVIEW-v1]. Your job is to try to falsify it before it is submitted. Treat the claim below as an unverified hypothesis from a stranger. Do not be polite at the expense of accuracy. Check: (1) Graveyard check via check_against_graveyard; (2) Counter-evidence check via get_conflicting_evidence and search_studies; (3) Biological fidelity tier check (Tier 1..4); (4) Quantitative check of PMIDs, verbatim quotes, and sample sizes; (5) Output a structured block starting with [OPENISLET-REVIEW-v1] and quoting 'Claim reviewed: <one-sentence summary>'.

tools.name: get_blueprint_overview
tools.description: Read the OpenIslet blueprint (Islet-1) in plain English. Start here. Sections: summary (what it is), tests (the five tests a design must pass), designs (Design A, Design B, and the challenger Design X / Islet-X), roadmap (the six stages), versions (draft and locked versions), help (how to contribute). Set detail to "full" to add the technical text from the concise specification.

section.description: Which part to read. Default: summary.

design.description: Read one design. X separates the scored grid challenger from the unmaterialized molecular proposal.

detail.description: "plain" (default) is plain English. "full" adds the technical text.

version.description: Which version to read: "draft" (the default, the open draft), "latest" (the newest locked version) or a name such as "islet-1.0".

tools.name: list_versions
tools.description: List the versions of Islet-1: the open draft (which changes all the time), the locked versions (frozen and citable, each with a DOI) and the planned lock dates. A new locked version is planned every three months. Use it to say which version you are working from.

tools.name: search_studies
tools.description: Search the studies and findings behind the blueprint by words, gene, test, direction or year. Returns studies, each with its best-matching findings and a PubMed link. Findings are grouped by the five tests (1, 2A, 2B, 3, 4, 5); the grouping is the project's, not the paper's. Results come in pages: pass next_offset as offset to read more.

query.description: Words to look for, for example "CD47 hypoxia" or "granzyme B inhibitor".

source_scope.description: Default empirical excludes reviews, summaries and superseded preprints. reviews or all includes contextual records without treating them as primary evidence.

gene.description: A gene symbol, for example CD47, B2M or PD-L1. Only findings that name this gene.

test.description: Only findings that bear on this test.

direction.description: protective: the change improved the outcome. deleterious: it impaired it. neutral: no clear difference.

human_only.description: Only studies that used human cells or people.

version.description: Which version to read: "draft" (the default, the open draft), "latest" (the newest locked version) or a name such as "islet-1.0".

tools.name: get_study
tools.description: Get one study by PubMed ID: its title and source, the groups that were compared (with any gene edits), every finding extracted from it, and the exact quote where the publisher's rules allow it. Where a quote is withheld, the location in the paper and a fingerprint are given so it can be checked against the paper.

pmid.description: A PubMed ID such as 39326417, or "PMID:39326417". A title also works and returns the closest studies.

version.description: Which version to read: "draft" (the default, the open draft), "latest" (the newest locked version) or a name such as "islet-1.0".

tools.name: get_conflicting_evidence
tools.description: For one gene, show the findings where changing it improved the outcome next to the findings where it impaired the outcome, best evidence first, with any known trade-offs across tests. Use it to test a claim about a gene, because it shows both sides.

gene.description: A gene symbol such as CD47, B2M, TYK2 or PD-L1.

per_side.description: How many findings to show on each side. Default 6.

version.description: Which version to read: "draft" (the default, the open draft), "latest" (the newest locked version) or a name such as "islet-1.0".

tools.name: check_against_graveyard
tools.description: The Idea Graveyard lists ideas that the evidence argues against ("dead end": a design scores zero in the model) or that carry a risk that needs a check. These are checks on paper, not lab results. Mode "exact" checks a design built from named modules (give design "A", "B" or "X", and/or a list of modules, and optionally the number of base edits). It uses the same rules as the scoring program and says which parts were not named. Mode "suggest" takes an idea in words and returns the nearest rules, clearly labelled as suggestions, because words are not modules. Mode "list" shows every module. If mode is left out, it is chosen from what you give.

design.description: A named design from the blueprint (A, B, or emergent challenger X). Modules you also give replace the matching part.

modules.description: Design module ids, one per part of the design (use mode "list" to see them).

base_edits.description: Total base or prime edits. Worked out from the modules if left out.

idea.description: An idea in your own words, for suggest mode.

version.description: Which version to read: "draft" (the default, the open draft), "latest" (the newest locked version) or a name such as "islet-1.0".

tools.name: get_open_questions
tools.description: List the known weak spots and open questions in the blueprint, each with how it could be settled. Check here before writing an Islet Improvement Proposal (IIP), so effort is not duplicated, and say which question an IIP answers.

test.description: Only questions that affect this test.

design.description: Only questions that affect this design.

version.description: Which version to read: "draft" (the default, the open draft), "latest" (the newest locked version) or a name such as "islet-1.0".

tools.name: get_layer_atlas
tools.description: Read one of the five blueprint layers: "evidence" (the 1,151-study Type 1 Diabetes Context–Evidence Graph), "dna" (the edits checked against the real genome), "proteins" (3D structures and fits), "tissue" (oxygen and blood-sugar simulations) or "patient" (the patient-matching simulation). Without an item it gives an outline. With an item (a name from the outline, with dots to go deeper) it gives that part. These are computer analyses and none has been tested in the lab. Matching your own genotype is not offered yet.

item.description: A part of the layer, for example "summary". Use dots to go deeper.

version.description: Which version to read: "draft" (the default, the open draft), "latest" (the newest locked version) or a name such as "islet-1.0".

tools.name: get_contributions
tools.description: See who has contributed to the blueprint and what each contribution changed, in words. There are no scores or rankings: a person decides each outcome and says why. Everything is public. Model names are reported by contributors and are never shown as verified.

status.description: An outcome or where it stands: changed the blueprint, ruled out a dead end, added evidence, raised an open question, kept for later, not taken up, already covered, waiting for review, needs work or withdrawn.

version.description: Only contributions written against, or landed in, this version, for example "islet-1-draft" or "islet-1.0".

tools.name: get_submission_status
tools.description: Where a submission stands: queued (the software checks are done), then set aside or reviewed in the weekly review, and the decision. All submissions are public, so this needs no sign-in.

id.description: The record id or issue number, for example IIP-0042 or 42.

tools.name: get_review_prompt
tools.description: Builds the prompt for the blind review from the draft: the public reviewer template with the draft's claim, evidence and proposed change in it, word for word. Give it to the person exactly as it is, to paste into a brand-new chat. Do not do the review in this chat. Nothing is stored or sent.

tools.name: check_draft
tools.description: A dry run of the checks a submission goes through. Give the draft file and the blind review file. It reports whether they follow the templates and meet the basic rules, then checks the cited papers and quotes against the OpenIslet record, whether the review is about the same claim, related Idea Graveyard rules, duplicates and links, and says what to fix. Nothing is stored or sent. Use it before submit_proposal.

draft.description: The whole draft file (Markdown), from the "Draft" prompt.

review.description: The whole blind review file (Markdown), from the reviewer prompt.

ai_tools.description: The AI tool and effort used for the draft and for the review, if not already named in the files.

consent.description: True if the person agrees the Islet Improvement Proposal (IIP) and review will be published openly under CC BY 4.0.

written_against.description: The version the draft was written against. Default: the current draft.

tools.name: submit_proposal
tools.description: Send an Islet Improvement Proposal (IIP) and its blind review to the public queue. Software checks it straight away (its format, the Idea Graveyard rules, and its quotes against the studies OpenIslet already holds). A person looks the papers up on PubMed and reviews the science in the weekend review. Everything is published openly under CC BY 4.0 and names the GitHub account that signs in. Only call this after the person has agreed, the review says Supported or Partly supported, and check_draft is clean. Lead the person through the steps first (see the server instructions) and get a clear yes to publishing before you call it. If the person is signed in with GitHub, the public issue is opened now. If not, nothing is made public: the checked files are saved for 24 hours and you get a link to the web form on openislet.org with both files already filled in. Give that link to the person exactly as it is, so they can press "Continue with GitHub & Submit" themselves. Until the public queue opens this checks the files and reports that submissions open soon, and sends nothing. The optional contributor details are shown as stated by the person, never as verified.

consent.description: True only if the person agrees to publish the IIP and review openly under CC BY 4.0.

idempotency_key.description: Any unique string. A retry with the same key never posts twice.

contributor.description: Optional details the person chooses to share. They are plain text, shown as stated by the contributor and never as verified.

name.description: A display name the person wants shown (80 characters at most).

orcid.description: An ORCID iD such as 0000-0002-1825-0097, if the person wants it shown.

x.description: An X handle (letters, numbers and underscores, 15 at most), if the person wants it shown.

stage1_lab_desk_and_layer_simulation_ext.note: Input contracts for the blueprint repository's layer scripts and wet-lab ingestor. The connector does not serve them; its 13 tools are listed above.
